meta.description: Detect allele-specific chromatin accessibility from ATAC-seq using WASP, GATK ASEReadCounter, or RASQUAL. Use when mapping cis-regulatory genetic variants from heterozygous SNPs, validating GWAS variant function with allelic imbalance, building a phased within-peak ASE analysis, or detecting reference-allele mapping bias before downstream analysis.

scientific_integrity.detail: No output fabricated study identifiers, sample sizes, p-values, effect sizes, or experimental claims; every numerical result was read from the bounded public runs or deterministic fixtures.

practice_boundaries.detail: The skill remains a research analysis workflow and makes no patient-specific diagnosis, treatment recommendation, or clinical prescription.

methodological_ground.detail: A valid BED4 input with two distinct genomic intervals sharing one display name is silently collapsed into one peak/phase-set test. The helper groups only by the display label and phase set, so unrelated coordinates can be pooled, the SNP-count threshold can be crossed incorrectly, and significance can be manufactured.

code_usability.detail: The 14-test shipped suite passed; the real bounded WASP-to-GATK workflow produced a sorted indexed one-sample BAM and 953 non-empty GATK rows; and the real two-feature RASQUAL workflow produced 166 validated association rows.

functional_suitability.note: All inherited core workflows are now implemented and correct on their tested paths, but peak identity is not coordinate-safe when BED4 labels repeat.

reliability.note: Sample, schema, empty, staging, and reuse failures are explicit; duplicate peak labels remain an accepted valid input that silently changes the statistical grouping.

performance_context.note: Progressive references and bounded executable drivers are efficient; the full WASP path remains inherently expensive but is scientifically motivated and thread-configurable.

agent_usability.note: Method routing, outputs, stop conditions, and external-only branches are clear, while the undocumented uniqueness assumption on BED4 names can mislead an agent using ordinary peak labels.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger language, readable status outputs, and actionable errors support use and recovery; no warning tells users that repeated BED4 names are unsafe.

security.note: No credentials, raw-code execution, unquoted shell paths, unsafe overwrite, or broad destructive operation was found in the candidate.

maintainability.note: Three scripts, focused references, and 14 deterministic tests are well separated; the regression suite omits coordinate identity for duplicate peak labels.

agent_specific.note: Triggering, progressive disclosure, composition, idempotency, and external-route escape hatches are strong, with one hidden input invariant blocking readiness.

inputs.label: Bounded public WASP-to-GATK and peak aggregation
inputs.note: The exact candidate ran end to end on ENCODE/1000 Genomes chr1:1-5 Mb data with an explicitly bounded PS=1 derivative, while the unmodified PS-free VCF was rejected and cleaned up.

assertions.text: The pipeline retains exactly the BAM target sample before heterozygous filtering.
assertions.note: The filtered VCF contained only NA12878 and 3,542 target heterozygous variants.

assertions.text: The final WASP BAM is coordinate sorted, sample-read-grouped, indexed, and non-empty.
assertions.note: The final BAM reported SO=coordinate, one NA12878 SM, a readable index, and 268,176 reads.

assertions.text: GATK ASEReadCounter emits non-empty scientifically inspectable rows.
assertions.note: GATK emitted 953 rows, including 28 rows at total depth at least 30.

assertions.text: The peak output has the declared phase-oriented schema and meaningful values.
assertions.note: One row was written with all ten declared columns after consuming a 3,542-row haplotype map.

assertions.text: The public PS-free input is not silently treated as one phase block.
assertions.note: The source VCF without PS failed before promotion and left neither a final output nor a temporary sibling.

inputs.label: Peak orientation, phase blocks, schemas, and duplicate labels
inputs.note: Orientation, phase separation, statuses, empty outputs, malformed schemas, and paths with spaces passed, but two distinct intervals sharing BED4 label dup were collapsed into one significant two-SNP test.

assertions.text: Opposite locus-specific REF labels are oriented to the same biological haplotype before pooling.
assertions.note: The shared phase block produced haplotype counts 180:20 and a significant-imbalance status.

assertions.text: Different phase sets remain separate and retain non-significant or underpowered statuses.
assertions.note: A second phase block remained a separate row with two SNPs and non-significant status.

assertions.text: Empty and no-overlap inputs return the exact stable ten-column schema.
assertions.note: Both cases returned header-only tables without raw tracebacks.

assertions.text: Malformed ASE input fails actionably without creating a misleading result.
assertions.note: The helper exited 2, named the missing ASE columns, and did not create the requested output.

assertions.text: Distinct genomic peak intervals cannot be pooled solely because their optional BED4 labels match.
assertions.note: Two disjoint one-SNP intervals named dup became one row with snp_count 2 and significant_imbalance.

inputs.label: Target-only genotype, identity, staging, and reuse guards
inputs.note: Synthetic valid BAM/VCF boundaries and the real run confirmed target-only selection, identity mismatch refusal, staged cleanup, quoted paths, and existing-output refusal.

assertions.text: A target-homozygous site is excluded even when another VCF sample is heterozygous.
assertions.note: The two-sample fixture stopped with no target heterozygous SNPs rather than leaking donor2 heterozygosity.

assertions.text: BAM and VCF sample-identity mismatch stops before analysis.
assertions.note: A donor2-only VCF failed with the exact one-sample match error and exit 65.

assertions.text: Failures after staging remove temporary and final output paths.
assertions.note: Both the target-empty fixture and PS-free public run left no output or matching temporary sibling.

assertions.text: Existing output directories are refused rather than reused or overwritten.
assertions.note: The synthetic and public reruns both refused the existing path with the documented exit 73.

assertions.text: Paths containing spaces survive the complete public workflow.
assertions.note: The real input and output directories with spaces completed through WASP, GATK, and aggregation.

inputs.label: Two-feature public RASQUAL execution and BH family
inputs.note: The exact driver executed both public matrix rows and returned 166 finite association rows; the global BH vector was independently recomputed and matched.

assertions.text: Two feature records map to distinct one-based binary-matrix rows.
assertions.note: C11orf21 used row 1 and TSPAN32 used row 2 in both the dry-run plan and real summary.

assertions.text: The real run produces results for every executable feature.
assertions.note: Each feature produced 83 rows, for 166 association rows total.

assertions.text: Raw and adjusted probabilities are finite and lie within zero and one.
assertions.note: All 332 probability values passed finite range checks.

assertions.text: BH adjustment covers the complete reported two-feature test family.
assertions.note: An independent BH recomputation across all 166 raw p-values matched every emitted adjusted p-value.

assertions.text: Dimension, zero-feature, path-array, and output-reuse boundaries are enforced.
assertions.note: Wrong matrix bytes failed, a zero-feature row was recorded as skipped, argument arrays preserved paths, and an existing output directory was refused.

inputs.label: External-only routing, claims, provenance, and exact identity
inputs.note: The candidate identity, pinned provider commit and blobs, external-only MatrixEQTL/QuASAR boundaries, and conditioned scientific claims all passed independent static checks.

assertions.text: The audited candidate exactly matches the declared deterministic content identity.
assertions.note: Eleven files and the 1,099-byte ordinal manifest hashed to 4310ddfa1d9ed178f033ad42e77e0772ddadd3c4905dd1e9bcef8b6289a24103.

assertions.text: Provider provenance is pinned to a clean commit with canonical Git blob identities.
assertions.note: The provider checkout was clean at d91ed3d and all three documented blob IDs resolved exactly.

assertions.text: Checkout-normalized hashes are distinguished from canonical source identity.
assertions.note: The provenance page explicitly labels newline-normalized checkout SHA-256 values and treats Git blobs as canonical.

assertions.text: MatrixEQTL and QuASAR are represented only as external routing options.
assertions.note: The skill and method reference explicitly state that no executable workflow or data/output contract is shipped for either route.

assertions.text: Phasing, cohort multiplicity, power, and concordance claims remain within tested evidence.
assertions.note: Phasing is scoped to pooling, study-specific FDR/permutation is required, and unsupported fixed p-value, power-fold, and concordance percentages are absent.

key_strengths: The bounded public WASP-to-GATK workflow now enforces target identity, coordinate order, read groups, indexing, non-empty GATK output, staging, and safe reuse semantics.
Peak aggregation correctly orients opposite REF labels to a shared haplotype, keeps phase sets separate, and emits stable empty, error, and status schemas on the tested unique-name inputs.
The RASQUAL driver executed two public matrix rows, produced 166 finite association rows, and matched an independent complete-family BH recomputation.
MatrixEQTL and QuASAR claims are honestly bounded to external routing, while canonical provider blobs and checkout-normalization caveats preserve provenance.

recommendations.title: ASA-009: key peak groups by coordinates, not BED label
recommendations.problem: Two distinct BED intervals with the same optional BED4 name are silently pooled into one peak/phase-set row. This can inflate SNP count and coverage and create a significant result that neither interval supports independently.
recommendations.root_cause: map_variants_to_peaks carries only the display label into evaluate_groups, which groups on peak and phaseSet and discards chromosome/start/end identity.
recommendations.fix: Carry chromosome, start, and end through the intersection and group on coordinate identity plus phaseSet; treat the BED4 name as display metadata only, or reject duplicate names explicitly. Add a regression with two disjoint one-SNP intervals sharing a label and require two underpowered rows.
